item.title: #120 Aver AI-Native Programming Language with Szymon Teżewski
item.description:
We dive into the new Aver programming language with its creator, Szymon Teżewski: The AI-native language where code explains itself.

Aver is a language where every function carries its intent, side effects are visible in the type system, and tests are executable specs next to the code. The optimization target is the reviewer, not the generator.

  • Agent Languages

item.description: Adam Fraser is a core contributor to Scala ZIO. He joins us to chat about improvements in ZIO 2 and how we can grow adoption.

item.title: #44 Tired of Getting N+1'd by Your ORM? A Chat With Alexander Ioffe.
item.description: We chat with Alexander Ioffe, maintainer of the Quill library, about database access approaches and Scala metaprogramming.

item.title: #43 Rúnar Bjarnason is Jackhammering the Foundations of Programming
item.description: We've mentioned the futuristic Unision programming language many times but now we dive deep with one of the co-founders.

item.title: #42 The answer to life, the universe, and everything is an abstraction with Viktor Klang
item.description: The legendary Viktor Klang chats with Bruce & James about information loss, reactive, emergence, and many other mind expanding topics.

item.title: #41 "Never gonna give you up" (FP that is) with Wiem Zine Elabidine
item.description:
Bruce and James hear about Wiem's journey in Functional Programming, her contributions to Scala ZIO, and how she never gave up despite the challenges she faced.

Resources & links

  • never gave up

item.title: #40 Poisoned Agile with Barry Hawkins
item.description: Bruce and James chat with Barry Hawkins about software methodologies, their triumphs and abuses.

item.title: #39 Cracking the Company Culture Conundrum with Sharon Schmidt
item.description: According to James, Heroku had the best company culture / vibe of anywhere he has worked. Bruce & James talk with Sharon Schmidt who is in large part responsible for creating that magical experience.

item.title: #38 Databases are Insufficient with Jonas Bonér
item.description:
James rants about databases with Jonas Bonér, CEO of Lightbend and creator of Akka. Bruce & James also learn about the actor model, Reactive, and Akka Serverless.

Resources & links

  • Jonas Bonér

item.title: #37 The Future of Everything with Paul Snively
item.description:
Paul Snively helps us see the future of programming. Spoiler: It's Typed & Functional.

Referenced talks

Types vs. Tests: An Epic Battle?

Type Systems - The Good, Bad and Ugly

Resources & links

  • Types vs. Tests: An Epic Battle?
  • Type Systems - The Good, Bad and Ugly

item.title: #36 The Freedom of Structured Unconferences
item.description: Bruce describes his multi-decade journey running conferences and how letting go of control, while still having a structure, has led to conferences where attendees connect in meaningful ways.

item.title: #35 The Pattern of Design Patterns
item.description: As usual, Bruce & James try to figure out monads & type classes. Then something new, as they go meta on design patterns.

item.title: #34 Fear, Uncertainty, and Monads with Dick Wall
item.description: FEE, FOO, FUD, and FUM (Fear, Uncertainty, and Monads) - Scala Giant, Dick Wall, joins Bruce and James to talk about life, work, and Functional Programming.

item.title: #33 Rethinking "Thinking in Objects"
item.description: Object Oriented Programming might just be a series of solutions to self-created problems.

item.title: #32 Adopting Kotlin & FP with Katie Levy
item.description:
Katie Levy joins Bruce & James to talk about how to help teams adopt Kotlin and Functional Programming.

Resources & links

  • Katie Levy

item.title: #31 "ZIO's not a library it's a state of mind" with Kit Langton
item.description: Bruce and James' coauthor Bill Frasure, joins to talk with Kit Langton, creator of ZIO Magic and many other magical ZIO tools & libraries.

item.title: #30 Programming in (not with) Scala 3 but with Bill Venners
item.description: Bruce and James chat with their long time friend Bill Venners about Scala 3 and the updates to his "Programming in Scala" book.

item.title: #29 Contemplating Computer Cognition with Julie Amundson
item.description: Bruce and James chat with their friend Julie Amundson about AI, Machine Learning, and many related complexities.  They explore what the journey is like for Data Scientists at medium / large companies where everything from data access to productionizing models, has challenges.  Also we learn about the Metaflow system Julie's team built to make this journey smoother at Netflix.

item.title: #28 PREP - Performant, Reliable, Expressive, and Productive
item.description: Bruce, James, and their friend Bill are working on a new book about systems that are Performant, Reliable, Expressive, and Productive. This episode explores those themes with some significant detours along the way.

item.title: #27 Side-Effects of a Scala 3 Release
item.description: With the eminent release of Scala 3, we chat about the language changes, effect systems (ZIO), and reliability.

item.title: #26 Dependency Injection - Why Do We Even...
item.description: All about Dependency Injection, why we do it, and why James thinks it is terrible.

item.title: #25 No Good Build Tools. Blocked on Reactive.
item.description: Once again we lament build tools. Then we get blocked talking about Reactive, async, non-blocking, actors, and concurrency.

item.title: #24 Vulnerability & Additive Hiring with Dianne Marsh
item.description:
Bruce & James have a delightful chat with long-time friend Dianne Marsh about changing tech culture to be more vulnerable and diverse.

Note: The Non-Violent Communication trainer mentioned in the episode is Karl Steyaert.

item.title: #23 The Modern Java Platform - 2021 Edition
item.description: James shares about a blog he posted this week titled: "The Modern Java Platform - 2021 Edition"

item.title: #22 Be the Kindness You Want to See in the Programming World
item.description: Special guest Oli joins us to chat about Recursion Schemes, tech conferences, podcasts, and kindness.

item.title: #21 Statically-Dynamic Programming or Dynamically-Static Programming? And Death by 1000 Language Quirks
item.description: James is a Dynamic Programming Language Denier but realizes only a part of his code is actually statically typed. And programming languages so full of quirks that you have to hold the quick reference book in your teeth.

item.title: #20 Cultures (not the petri dish variety) & Developer Marketing (also not the petri dish variety)
item.description:
Culture - the hidden force that sometimes reveals itself through code reviews. What is it & how does it form / change?

Also, Developer Marketing and how most companies do it wrong.

item.title: #19 Technology Evolution & Adoption - Why So Slow?
item.description: Change happens, but slowwwwly. How can we accelerate the adoption of new & better programming language features? Should we?

item.title: #18 "But Will it Scale?" and Other Illusions of Control
item.description: Software architectures, organizational management, hiring practices, and many other normal part of life give us an illusion of control.  But is there another way?

item.title: #17 The Problem with Gradle; Java 11; SemVer Isn't
item.description:
Bruce and James have struggled with Gradle for years and Bruce this week blogged about some of his gripes: The Problem with Gradle. This prompted a lengthy response from Cédric Champeau.

James has mostly stuck to Java 8 and Bruce is exploring Java 11.

Finally, James rants about SemVer for the 3.1.4'th time.

Resources & links

  • The Problem with Gradle
  • a lengthy response from Cédric Champeau

item.title: #16 Kotlin for Scala Devs. Reflection is the Devil. Meta-Programming.
item.description: James, as a Scala "True Believer," talks about his experiences with Kotlin and how they compare to Scala. Then he switches gears to rant about runtime reflection which leads to a deeper conversation about meta-programming and alternatives to runtime reflection.

item.title: #15 Atomic Kotlin Done! Cloud Events. TestContainers / Serverless Cassandra. Scala ZIO CLI.
item.description: Bruce shares exciting news about completing the Atomic Kotlin book. The rest is a mishmash of topics related to newsworthy announcements including Spring Boot Cloud Event support, Serverless + TestContainer + Kubernetes Cassandra support, and Scala ZIO CLI.

item.title: #14 Poly-Polymorphism
item.description: Most developers have been exposed to inheritance based polymorphism but there are other ways to deal with overlapping functionality. In this episode we talk about ad-hoc polymorphism, parametric polymorphism, and type classes.

item.title: #12 The Rise of Python & (Unrelated) Making Illegal States Unrepresentable
item.description: Python usage surpasses Java to second place on the Tiobe Index (behind C). Is developer productivity the primary driver? We then switch gears to talk about the concept of "Making Illegal States Unrepresentable" where James continues his crusade against the Builder Pattern.

item.title: #11 Small talk about Smalltalk
item.description:
Our friend Joey Gibson joins us to talk about Smalltalk, the well known grandfather of Object Oriented Programming.  James is assigned some homework to get a Smalltalk web app running on Google Cloud Run, which he did (after recording). Check out the source

Resources & links

  • https://github.com/jamesward/hello-pharo

item.title: #10 Gazing Into the Programming Crystal Ball and Can Organizations Adopt Inner Source?
item.description: We start off discussing what the future of programming might be... Can developers stop thinking about resource limitations?  Can we make the "right path" easy?  Then we dive into Inner Source and the organizational & cultural challenges with adopting it.

item.title: #9 Buildpacks, Containers, Kubernetes, Happy Path Programming, Rust, and gRPC
item.description: We start off talking about Cloud Native Buildpacks and Containers which of-course leads to James trying to explain Kubernetes.  Then we dive into what "Happy Path Programming" means and how, while the term is somewhat derogatory, it is what we ultimately want.  We end with a discussion about Bruce's recent explorations into Rust and gRPC.

item.title: #8 Kotlin Revisited with Cedric Beust
item.description: Long-time Java author & expert, Cedric Beust, joins us to revisit some of the topics from our Kotlin episodes.  We talk more deeply about checked exceptions, null safety, the builder pattern, build systems, and of-course Monads.

item.title: #7 Why Adopt New Technology? And Monads! Monads! Monads!
item.description: What are the reasons to adopt or migrate to a new technology?  What prevents you from doing so?  We explore that question and the differences between green-field and brown-field.  Then we finally dive deep into Monads trying to conquer the Curse of the Monad.

item.title: #6 The Crusade Against Custom Declarative Languages and Meta-Bike-Shedding
item.description: James officially launches his crusade against custom declarative languages and then we bike-shed about bike-shedding; exploring ways to make decisions for trivial problems.

item.title: #5 Developer Productivity, Non-Violent Agile, and Organizational Structures
item.description: We begin by talking about personal developer productivity but then expand the scope to "collective" / team productivity.  This leads us to grapple with some challenging ideas around Agile, non-violent communication, organization structures, diversity, and inclusion.

item.title: #4 Why is Developer Experience Often Terrible?
item.description: In this episode we discuss things that are often overlooked in developer experience and what underlying values make developer experience an afterthought.

item.title: #3 Nulls, ADTs, and Code Formatting
item.description: A bike-shedless discussion about nulls, algebraic data types, and code formatting.

item.title: #2 More Kotlin!
item.description: In episode 2 we continue the conversation about Kotlin, things we enjoy and things that could be better.

item.title: #1 Adventures in Kotlin
item.description: In our first episode we discuss features of the Kotlin programming language that we like.
